instructions.question: Does the current executable application source load or call the target package as a library? Dynamic require/import with a known target package name counts. A command in package scripts, a build tool or framework plugin configuration is tooling, not application runtime use. A package name containing 'tool' does not make library code tooling. Comments, documentation and string mentions alone are not executable use. Loading the target module and exporting that loaded module counts as use. Exporting only a package-name string does not.

instructions.question: Does a current package script invoke the target command, or does a current build/test/lint/framework configuration activate the target as a tool or plugin? Application source loading a library with require/import is runtime use, not tooling merely because its name contains 'tool'. Comments, documentation, declarations and string mentions without an executable consumer are not tool invocation. A configuration that loads the target module and places its plugin instance in the exported plugins list establishes tooling use. An exported plugins list containing only package-name strings requires a demonstrated loader; the property name alone does not prove activation. A locally resolved map or loop that loads the target and registers its plugin instance also counts; deployment execution need not be proved.

Comments, documentation and string mentions alone are not executable use. Loading the target module and exporting that loaded module counts as use. Exporting only a package-name string does not.

instructions.question: Does a current package script invoke the target command, or does a current build/test/lint/framework configuration activate the target as a tool or plugin? Application source loading a library with require/import is runtime use, not tooling merely because its name contains 'tool'. Comments, documentation, declarations and string mentions without an executable consumer are not tool invocation. A configuration that loads the target module and places its plugin instance in the exported plugins list establishes tooling use. An exported plugins list containing only package-name strings requires a demonstrated loader; the property name alone does not prove activation. A locally resolved map or loop that loads the target and registers its plugin instance also counts; deployment execution need not be proved.

instructions.question: Does this record indicate a potential consumer of the target whose use is unresolved? Examples: exporting a target package name for an unavailable consumer, an unresolved dynamic loader that could load it, or an explicit note that required deployment/startup/framework implementation is missing or unverified. A resolved runtime invocation or activated tool/plugin is already usage, not an unresolved consumer. An inert comment proposing future use or describing removed use does not by itself indicate an unresolved consumer. Evaluate only this supplied record; do not speculate about unrelated files or hypothetical deployments. Comments reporting missing required code are gap hints, not proof of use. A proposal that is not implemented describes future use, not a missing current consumer. Exporting a package-name string or an object/list containing it exposes a potential consumer; if that consumer is unavailable it remains unresolved, even without an explicit missing-consumer comment. A local string used only for printing or formatting, with no export or transfer to an unavailable consumer, is display text and does not create a consumer gap. Passing the name to a consumer whose implementation is unavailable remains unresolved. Exporting a loaded module remains resolved usage.
